The USA justice system is based on deterrence. That means that punishments for crime are meant to be an example to scare every law abiding citizen into compliance. Criminals are getting punished only to scare everyone else, not for their own good.
My little European country doesn't have enough citizens to be able to throw people away. Our justice system is largely rehabilitative. Criminals are treated as people that the system have failed, and the reason they broke the law is what is addressed. For example, if they are poor and committed theft to afford food and housing, they will spend their time in prison learning a trade so that they can afford food and housing after they get out of jail. There are exceptions for the few individuals that genuinely cannot recover, but currently that is only somewhere between 7 and 30 people total, and they get reevaluated periodically.
A hacker is a bored clever nerd who could easily use their brain for the good of a country's people. They might have to pay off a large fine for damages for many years, but they'd be alive, and if the system works properly, they'd get to have fun with computers for a living.
